335	class AddCase:
336	    """Adding a printer, on the Add session the app sent in a recorded run: its
337	    full printer list, and the tools' answers for the printers the case names,
338	    checked as PrinterConversation::identify and ::add check them. A call about
339	    any other printer is answered as untested and reported."""
340	
341	    session = ADD["session"]
342	
343	    def __init__(self):
344	        self.added = []
345	        self.lookups = []  # printer_identify calls that drew cards, by turn
346	        self.identify_calls = []  # every printer_identify call, drawn or refused
347	        self.turn = 0
348	        self.untested = []
349	
350	    def tool(self, name, arguments):
351	        nozzle = arguments.get("nozzle")
352	        said = isinstance(nozzle, (int, float)) and nozzle > 0
353	        if name == "printer_identify":
354	            self.identify_calls.append(arguments)
355	            ids = list(dict.fromkeys(arguments.get("catalogIds", [])))
356	            unknown = [catalog_id for catalog_id in ids if catalog_id not in CATALOG]
357	            if unknown:
358	                return {"error": {"code": "unknown_printer", "message": f'"{unknown[0]}" is not on the printer list; copy it '
359	                                                                      "exactly from the printer list."}}, False
360	            if len(ids) > 3:
361	                return {"error": {"code": "too_many",
362	                                  "message": "More than three fit. Ask one question that narrows it down instead."}}, False
363	            if not all(catalog_id in IDENTIFIED for catalog_id in ids):
364	                self.untested += ids
365	                return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test has no answer for " + ", ".join(ids) + "."}}, False
366	            for catalog_id in ids:
367	                if said and nozzle not in IDENTIFIED[catalog_id]["nozzles"]:
368	                    return unknown_nozzle(IDENTIFIED[catalog_id]["nozzles"], CATALOG[catalog_id], nozzle), False
369	            self.lookups.append(self.turn)
370	            return {"printers": [IDENTIFIED[catalog_id] for catalog_id in ids]}, False
371	        if name == "printer_add":
372	            catalog_id = arguments.get("catalogId", "")
373	            if catalog_id in self.added:
374	                return {"error": {"code": "already_added", "message": "This conversation already added it."}}, False
375	            if catalog_id not in ADD["printer_add"]:
376	                self.untested.append(catalog_id)
377	                return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test has no answer for " + catalog_id + "."}}, False
378	            answer = ADD["printer_add"][catalog_id]
379	            if said and nozzle not in answer["printer"]["nozzles"]:
380	                return unknown_nozzle(answer["printer"]["nozzles"], CATALOG[catalog_id], nozzle), False
381	            self.added.append(catalog_id)
382	            return {"printer": {**answer["printer"], "nozzle": nozzle if said else answer["printer"]["nozzle"]}}, False
383	        if name == "printer_change" and not self.added:
384	            # PrinterConversation::preflight_tool, before anything is added.
385	            return {"error": {"code": "no_printer",
386	                              "message": "No printer is set up in this conversation yet: add one first."}}, False
387	        self.untested.append(name)
388	        return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test does not answer " + name + "."}}, False
389	
390	    def say(self, conversation, words):
391	        """The turn's last reply."""
392	        self.turn += 1
393	        start = len(conversation.log)
394	        conversation.say(words)
395	        replies = [line for line in conversation.log[start:] if line.startswith("assistant: ")]
396	        return replies[-1][len("assistant: "):] if replies else ""
397	
398	    def outcome(self, printer, reply):
399	        # Space at a line's end is not shown, the page trims each choice, and a
400	        # blank line before the choices draws the same chips.
401	        offered = "\n".join(line.rstrip() for line in reply.rstrip().splitlines() if line.strip()).endswith(CONNECT_OFFER)
402	        passed = self.added == [printer] and offered
403	        detail = ("added" if self.added == [printer] else f"added {self.added or 'nothing'}") + \
404	                 ("; offered to connect" if offered else "; NO CONNECT OFFER: " + repr(reply[-120:]))
405	        if self.untested:
406	            detail += "; untested " + ", ".join(self.untested)
407	        return passed, detail

477	def last_reply(conversation, words=None, note=None):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Printer panel conversations against the live model, without the app.

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt (printerInstructions.ts),
five printer tools and the four settings tools, and the chat. This script sends the model the same
requests the app sends, answers the tools the way the app answers them for a
fixed printer, and checks what the model does. A case is a short scripted
conversation; each run of it is one sample of a model that answers
differently each time, so a case is run many times and the result is a count.

What the app sends, reproduced here:
  - instructions: rendered from printerInstructions.ts by render_prompt.mjs,
    so an edit to the prompt is tested without building anything;
  - tools: printer_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the printer panel
    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
  - input: earlier turns as the app replays them -- each assistant message's
    words, then the tool calls it made with their results, as function_call
    (no item id) and function_call_output -- then this turn's message, then
    this turn's calls and results (AgentHost::make_agent_request,
    OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input). A call the app refused before it ran
    (bad arguments) was never recorded, so it is not replayed.
The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs,
except which model answers them.

Usage:
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py
      [--runs N] [--must-pass N] [--case NAME] [--jobs 5] [--verbose]
      [--model NAME [--endpoint URL] [--key-env NAME] [--provider HOST]...]

Prompt changes are evaluated on DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to
the hosts that answer an app note (MODEL, PROVIDERS; decided 2026-09-28), and
on nothing else. --model tries another model through a Responses API endpoint,
with its key in the variable --key-env names, for comparing models, not for
judging a prompt change. The judge stays on OpenAI
(OPENAI_API_KEY) whichever model answers, so counts are judged alike.

Without --runs, the cases run share RUN_BUDGET conversations: 5 runs each for
20 cases, fewer when there are more, never more than MAX_RUNS for one case.

Exit code 0 when every case passes at least --must-pass of its runs
(default: all of them), 1 otherwise. Needs python3 and node, and the page's
npm install (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/node_modules) for esbuild.
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
# The model prompts are judged on (decided 2026-09-28): DeepSeek V4 Flash on
# OpenRouter, served only by the hosts that answer an app note -- the others
# render the app's developer messages so that the model replies with nothing
# (README, "Another model").
MODEL = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash"
ENDPOINT = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses"
KEY_ENV = "OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
PROVIDERS = ["Alibaba", "Novita", "Baidu", "AtlasCloud"]
# The judge stays on OpenAI whichever model answers, so counts are judged alike.
JUDGE_ENDPOINT = "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses"
JUDGE_MODEL = "gpt-5.5-2026-04-23"  # pinned, so a count moves only when the prompt does
# UTF-8 throughout: on Windows, Python otherwise reads text as the system code
# page and garbles "×" and curly quotes before the model sees them.
TOOLS = json.loads((HERE / "printer_tools.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN = 8
# Conversations one invocation runs by default, shared by the cases it runs,
# and the most one case gets from that share.
RUN_BUDGET = 100
MAX_RUNS = 20


def render(session, revision=None):
    """The page's system prompt and opening line for this session, from the
    checkout or, given a git revision, from the page's source at it."""
    node = shutil.which("node")
    if node is None:
        sys.exit("node is required to render the printer panel's prompt")
    result = subprocess.run([node, str(HERE / "render_prompt.mjs")] + ([revision] if revision else []), input=json.dumps(session),
                            capture_output=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
    return json.loads(result.stdout)


def post(body, key, endpoint=ENDPOINT):
    request = urllib.request.Request(endpoint, data=json.dumps(body).encode(), method="POST",
                                     headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + key, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    for attempt in range(5):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
                return json.load(response)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            if error.code not in (429, 500, 502, 503) or attempt == 4:
                raise RuntimeError(f"OpenAI {error.code}: {error.read().decode(errors='replace')[:500]}")
        except (urllib.error.URLError, ConnectionError):  # ConnectionError: a reset mid-response
            if attempt == 4:
                raise
        time.sleep(2 ** attempt)


def judge(log, question):
    """A yes or no about the conversation's last reply, from a stronger model,
    for what no string test can check. Returns (yes, why)."""
    schema = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["answer", "why"],
              "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}, "why": {"type": "string"}}}
    response = post({"model": JUDGE_MODEL, "store": False,
                     "instructions": "You read a chat between a 3D printing app's assistant and a person, and answer one "
                                     "question about it strictly as written, judging only what the messages say.",
                     "input": "\n".join(log) + "\n\nQuestion: " + question,
                     "text": {"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "verdict", "strict": True, "schema": schema}}},
                    os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], JUDGE_ENDPOINT)
    text = "".join(output_text(item) for item in response.get("output", []) if item.get("type") == "message")
    verdict = json.loads(text)
    return verdict["answer"] == "yes", verdict["why"]


# What every reply of every case must hold to, whatever the case checks.
INTERNAL_TERMS = re.compile(r"\b(profiles?|presets?|catalog(ue)?|catalogId|deviceId|printer_[a-z_]+)\b", re.IGNORECASE)


def reply_problems(reply):
    """How a reply breaks the prompt's rules for every reply: a "Choices:" line
    the page would show as text or draw wrongly (replyChoices.ts), or internal
    words."""
    problems = []
    lines = reply.rstrip().splitlines()
    found = re.search(r"(^|\s)Choices:(.*)$", lines[-1]) if lines else None
    if found is None and "Choices:" in reply:
        problems.append("CHOICES NOT ON THE LAST LINE")
    if found is not None:
        choices = [choice.strip() for choice in found.group(2).split("|") if choice.strip()]
        if not 2 <= len(choices) <= 4:
            problems.append(f"{len(choices)} CHOICES")
        if any(len(choice) >= 30 for choice in choices):
            problems.append("LONG CHOICE")
    if INTERNAL_TERMS.search(reply):
        problems.append("INTERNAL TERM " + repr(INTERNAL_TERMS.search(reply).group(0)))
    return problems


def dump(value):
    """JSON as the app writes it: compact, keys sorted."""
    return json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)


def output_text(item):
    return "".join(part.get("text", "") for part in item.get("content", []) if part.get("type") == "output_text")


def invalid_arguments(tool, arguments):
    """The registry's check before a tool runs, as far as the schema says."""
    schema = next((t["parameters"] for t in TOOLS if t["name"] == tool), None)
    if schema is None:
        return {"code": "unknown_tool", "message": f'There is no tool named "{tool}" here. Nothing was queued. Use one of the listed tools.'}
    missing = [name for name in schema.get("required", []) if name not in arguments]
    extra = [name for name in arguments if name not in schema.get("properties", {})]
    # ToolRegistry's valid_arguments for printer_connect: deviceId alone, or
    # hostType with a non-empty address.
    if tool == "printer_connect" and not extra and not (
            (set(arguments) == {"deviceId"} and arguments["deviceId"]) or
            (set(arguments) == {"hostType", "address"} and arguments["address"] and
             arguments["hostType"] in ("moonraker", "octoprint"))):
        return {"code": "invalid_arguments",
                "message": "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract. Give deviceId alone, or hostType with "
                           "the address the person gave. Without an address, ask the person for the one they open the "
                           "printer with in a browser, and call this once they give it."}
    if missing or extra:
        return {"code": "invalid_arguments",
                "message": f"Missing {missing}, unexpected {extra}. Nothing was queued. "
                           "Check the arguments against this tool's parameters and call it again."}
    # ToolRegistry's valid_settings_scope and valid_persist_as: each scope
    # takes exactly its own target, as an object.
    if tool.startswith("settings_"):
        scope, target = arguments.get("scope"), arguments.get("target")
        shapes = {"process": target is None,
                  "object": isinstance(target, dict) and set(target) == {"objectId"} and isinstance(target["objectId"], str),
                  "filament": isinstance(target, dict) and set(target) == {"preset"} and isinstance(target["preset"], str) and target["preset"],
                  "printer": isinstance(target, dict) and set(target) == {"preset"} and isinstance(target["preset"], str) and target["preset"]}
        persist = arguments.get("persistAs")
        if not shapes.get(scope, False) or (persist is not None and (scope == "object" or not isinstance(persist, str) or not persist)):
            message = ("The tool arguments do not match the registered contract. scope process takes no target; object "
                       "takes target.objectId; filament and printer take target.preset, the preset's name. persistAs is "
                       "not for object.")
            if isinstance(target, str):
                message += ' target must be a JSON object, not a string holding one: "target": {"preset": "<name>"}.'
            return {"code": "invalid_arguments", "message": message}
    return None


class Conversation:
    """One run of a case: the chat as the app would hold it."""

    def __init__(self, case, prompt, key, model, endpoint=ENDPOINT, providers=None):
        self.case, self.instructions, self.key, self.model = case, prompt["instructions"], key, model
        self.endpoint = endpoint
        # OpenRouter's hosts only, none else: which host serves a request decides
        # how a message it does not expect, such as the app's developer notes, is
        # rendered for the model.
        self.routing = {"provider": {"order": providers, "allow_fallbacks": False}} if providers else {}
        self.history = [{"role": "assistant", "content": prompt["opening"]}]  # the page's opening line
        self.log = ["assistant: " + prompt["opening"]]

    def say(self, words):
        """One turn: the person's words, then the model until it stops."""
        self.log.append("person: " + words)
        turn = self.history + [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": words}]}]
        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": words})
        self.respond(turn)

    def note(self, text):
        """The app's own line, as the developer, then the turn it starts
        (AgentHost::start_turn): the person has said nothing."""
        self.log.append("app: " + text)
        self.history.append({"role": "developer", "content": text})
        self.respond(list(self.history))

    def respond(self, turn):
        """The model until it stops."""
        refused = 0
        for _ in range(MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN):
            response = post({"model": self.model, "store": False, "parallel_tool_calls": False,
                             "instructions": self.instructions, "tools": getattr(self.case, "tools", TOOLS), "input": turn,
                             **self.routing},
                            self.key, self.endpoint)
            output = response.get("output", [])
            turn += output
            for reply in (output_text(item) for item in output if item.get("type") == "message"):
                if reply:
                    self.history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
                    self.log.append("assistant: " + reply)
            call = next((item for item in output if item.get("type") == "function_call"), None)
            if call is None:
                break
            arguments = json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}")
            self.log.append(f"tool: {call['name']} {json.dumps(arguments)}")
            problem = invalid_arguments(call["name"], arguments)
            if problem and refused < 2:
                refused += 1
                result, recorded = {"state": "failed", "error": problem}, False
            else:
                (result, _), recorded = self.case.tool(call["name"], arguments), True
            self.log.append("  -> " + dump(result))
            turn.append({"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call["call_id"], "output": dump(result)})
            if recorded:
                self.history += self.replayed(call, result)

    @staticmethod
    def replayed(call, result):
        return [{"type": "function_call", "call_id": call["call_id"], "name": call["name"], "arguments": call["arguments"]},
                {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call["call_id"], "output": dump(result)}]


# --- Cases -------------------------------------------------------------------


class ConnectBambu:
    """Connect a saved Bambu Lab A1 mini that is on the network in LAN mode.

    Passes when the model opens printer_connect's credential form for that
    printer.
    """

    name = "connect-bambu"
    session = {
        "mode": "connect", "printerName": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "blocks": [],
        "context": {"printer": {
            "name": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "model": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "nozzle": 0.4, "nozzles": [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
            "spools": [],
            "connected": False, "provider": "bambu"}},
    }
    # printer_connection_status as the app answered it for the fake printer.
    status = {"address": "", "candidates": [{"address": "127.0.0.1", "deviceId": "FAKE001", "name": "JusPrin Fake A1 mini"}],
              "hostType": "", "message": "", "nozzleMismatch": False, "provider": "bambu", "state": "not_configured"}

    def __init__(self):
        self.card = False
        self.refused = []
        self.other = []

    def tool(self, name, arguments):
        if name == "printer_connection_status":
            return self.status, False
        if name == "printer_connect":
            # The app accepts a listed printer's id or its name (preflight_tool).
            device = arguments.get("deviceId", "")
            if device in ("FAKE001", "JusPrin Fake A1 mini"):
                self.card = True
                return {"state": "credential_requested",
                        "message": "The app is waiting for the person to enter the printer credential locally."}, False
            self.refused.append(device)
            return {"error": {"code": "unknown_device",
                              "message": "Pass the deviceId of one of these printers in LAN mode: FAKE001 (JusPrin Fake A1 mini)."}}, False
        self.other.append(name)
        return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test does not answer " + name + "."}}, False

    def run(self, conversation):
        conversation.say("Yes, it is")
        if not self.card:
            conversation.say("Yes, connect it")
        detail = "card" if self.card else "NO CARD"
        if self.refused:
            detail += "; refused " + ", ".join(repr(device) for device in self.refused)
        if self.other:
            detail += "; also called " + ", ".join(self.other)
        return self.card, detail


ADD = json.loads((HERE / "add_session.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
CONNECT_OFFER = "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?\nChoices: Connect it | Not now"
CATALOG = {entry[0]: entry[1] for entry in ADD["session"]["context"]["printers"]}
# printer_identify's answers: the recorded ones, and the Bambu Lab A1 written
# from its profile (resources/profiles/BBL) in the same shape, for "bambu a1".
IDENTIFIED = {**ADD["printer_identify"],
              "BBL/Bambu Lab A1": {"alreadyYours": False, "brand": "Bambu Lab", "buildVolume": "256 × 256 × 256 mm",
                                   "catalogId": "BBL/Bambu Lab A1", "model": "A1", "nozzles": [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
                                   "assumed": {"filament": "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1", "nozzle": 0.4,
                                               "plate": "Textured PEI Plate"}}}


def unknown_nozzle(nozzles, model, nozzle):
    """PrinterConversation.cpp's unknown_nozzle refusal."""
    sizes = [f"{size:g}" for size in nozzles]
    return {"error": {"code": "unknown_nozzle",
                      "message": f"JusPrin supports {', '.join(sizes[:-1])} and {sizes[-1]} mm nozzles for {model}, but not "
                                 f"{nozzle:g} mm. Ask the person to check the nozzle marking or packaging; do not substitute "
                                 "a size."}}


class AddCase:
    """Adding a printer, on the Add session the app sent in a recorded run: its
    full printer list, and the tools' answers for the printers the case names,
    checked as PrinterConversation::identify and ::add check them. A call about
    any other printer is answered as untested and reported."""

    session = ADD["session"]

    def __init__(self):
        self.added = []
        self.lookups = []  # printer_identify calls that drew cards, by turn
        self.identify_calls = []  # every printer_identify call, drawn or refused
        self.turn = 0
        self.untested = []

    def tool(self, name, arguments):
        nozzle = arguments.get("nozzle")
        said = isinstance(nozzle, (int, float)) and nozzle > 0
        if name == "printer_identify":
            self.identify_calls.append(arguments)
            ids = list(dict.fromkeys(arguments.get("catalogIds", [])))
            unknown = [catalog_id for catalog_id in ids if catalog_id not in CATALOG]
            if unknown:
                return {"error": {"code": "unknown_printer", "message": f'"{unknown[0]}" is not on the printer list; copy it '
                                                                      "exactly from the printer list."}}, False
            if len(ids) > 3:
                return {"error": {"code": "too_many",
                                  "message": "More than three fit. Ask one question that narrows it down instead."}}, False
            if not all(catalog_id in IDENTIFIED for catalog_id in ids):
                self.untested += ids
                return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test has no answer for " + ", ".join(ids) + "."}}, False
            for catalog_id in ids:
                if said and nozzle not in IDENTIFIED[catalog_id]["nozzles"]:
                    return unknown_nozzle(IDENTIFIED[catalog_id]["nozzles"], CATALOG[catalog_id], nozzle), False
            self.lookups.append(self.turn)
            return {"printers": [IDENTIFIED[catalog_id] for catalog_id in ids]}, False
        if name == "printer_add":
            catalog_id = arguments.get("catalogId", "")
            if catalog_id in self.added:
                return {"error": {"code": "already_added", "message": "This conversation already added it."}}, False
            if catalog_id not in ADD["printer_add"]:
                self.untested.append(catalog_id)
                return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test has no answer for " + catalog_id + "."}}, False
            answer = ADD["printer_add"][catalog_id]
            if said and nozzle not in answer["printer"]["nozzles"]:
                return unknown_nozzle(answer["printer"]["nozzles"], CATALOG[catalog_id], nozzle), False
            self.added.append(catalog_id)
            return {"printer": {**answer["printer"], "nozzle": nozzle if said else answer["printer"]["nozzle"]}}, False
        if name == "printer_change" and not self.added:
            # PrinterConversation::preflight_tool, before anything is added.
            return {"error": {"code": "no_printer",
                              "message": "No printer is set up in this conversation yet: add one first."}}, False
        self.untested.append(name)
        return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test does not answer " + name + "."}}, False

    def say(self, conversation, words):
        """The turn's last reply."""
        self.turn += 1
        start = len(conversation.log)
        conversation.say(words)
        replies = [line for line in conversation.log[start:] if line.startswith("assistant: ")]
        return replies[-1][len("assistant: "):] if replies else ""

    def outcome(self, printer, reply):
        # Space at a line's end is not shown, the page trims each choice, and a
        # blank line before the choices draws the same chips.
        offered = "\n".join(line.rstrip() for line in reply.rstrip().splitlines() if line.strip()).endswith(CONNECT_OFFER)
        passed = self.added == [printer] and offered
        detail = ("added" if self.added == [printer] else f"added {self.added or 'nothing'}") + \
                 ("; offered to connect" if offered else "; NO CONNECT OFFER: " + repr(reply[-120:]))
        if self.untested:
            detail += "; untested " + ", ".join(self.untested)
        return passed, detail


class AddNamedModel(AddCase):
    """The person names one model plainly. Passes when that printer is added
    and the reply ends with the connect offer and its two choices."""

    name = "add-named-model"

    def run(self, conversation):
        reply = self.say(conversation, "bambu lab a1 mini")
        return self.outcome("BBL/Bambu Lab A1 mini", reply)


class AddChooseFromThree(AddCase):
    """A name that fits three models, then the person's choice, as a tap on its
    chip sends it. Passes when nothing is added before the choice, the chosen
    printer is, and the reply ends with the connect offer. Looking the chosen
    printer up again draws a second picture card; it is reported, not failed."""

    name = "add-choose-from-three"

    def run(self, conversation):
        self.say(conversation, "prusa mk4")
        asked_first = not self.added
        reply = self.say(conversation, "Prusa MK4S")
        passed, detail = self.outcome("Prusa/Prusa MK4S", reply)
        if not asked_first:
            passed, detail = False, "ADDED BEFORE ASKING; " + detail
        if 2 in self.lookups:
            detail += "; looked it up again"
        return passed, detail


class AddThenUndo(AddCase):
    """The person names one model, it is added, and they tap Undo on its
    receipt: the app removes it and says so in a note, then the model answers
    with nothing said. Passes when that reply adds nothing, drops the connect
    offer, and asks which printer they have."""

    name = "add-then-undo"
    printer = "BBL/Bambu Lab A1 mini"

    def run(self, conversation):
        self.say(conversation, "bambu lab a1 mini")
        if self.added != [self.printer]:
            return False, f"setup: added {self.added or 'nothing'}"
        name = ADD["printer_add"][self.printer]["printer"]["name"]
        # The app's note, word for word (PrinterConversation::undo_add).
        self.added = []  # the printer is gone; another add of it is a new one
        self.turn += 1
        start = len(conversation.log)
        conversation.note(f"The person tapped Undo on the receipt: {name} is removed and is no longer one of their printers.")
        replies = [line[len("assistant: "):] for line in conversation.log[start:] if line.startswith("assistant: ")]
        reply = replies[-1] if replies else ""
        problems = []
        if self.added:
            problems.append(f"ADDED {self.added} AGAIN")
        if not reply:
            problems.append("NO REPLY")
        if "Connect it" in reply:
            problems.append("STILL OFFERS TO CONNECT")
        if "?" not in reply:
            problems.append("ASKED NOTHING")
        detail = "; ".join(problems) or "asked again: " + repr(reply[-120:])
        if self.untested:
            detail += "; untested " + ", ".join(self.untested)
        return not problems, detail


def last_reply(conversation, words=None, note=None):
    """The last thing the model wrote in one turn: the person's words, or the
    app's note."""
    start = len(conversation.log)
    if note is None:
        conversation.say(words)
    else:
        conversation.note(note)
    replies = [line for line in conversation.log[start:] if line.startswith("assistant: ")]
    return replies[-1][len("assistant: "):] if replies else ""


def offers_done(reply):
    """Whether the page draws Done as the reply's one chip, reading the reply
    as splitChoices (replyChoices.ts) does: "Choices:" starting a word on the
    last line, with something said before it."""
    lines = reply.rstrip().splitlines()
    found = re.search(r"(^|\s)Choices:(.*)$", lines[-1]) if lines else None
    if found is None:
        return False
    said = "\n".join(lines[:-1]) + lines[-1][:found.start()]
    return [choice.strip() for choice in found.group(2).split("|") if choice.strip()] == ["Done"] and said.strip() != ""


def says_can_close(reply):
    return re.search(r"\b(?:can|may|safe to|okay to|ok to|feel free to)\s+close\s+(?:this\s+|the\s+|your\s+)?"
                     r"(?:chat|conversation)\b", reply, re.IGNORECASE) is not None


class Finishing:
    """When nothing is left to decide, tell the person they can close the chat."""

    def end(self, reply, detail):
        close = says_can_close(reply)
        choices = "Choices:" in reply
        detail += "; says to close" if close else "; NO CLOSE INSTRUCTION: " + repr(reply[-120:])
        if choices:
            detail += "; CHOICES OFFERED"
        return close and not choices, detail


class AddNotNowClose(Finishing, AddCase):
    """The person adds a printer and turns down connecting it. Passes when the
    reply to "Not now" says they can close the chat."""

    name = "add-not-now-close"

    def run(self, conversation):
        self.say(conversation, "bambu lab a1 mini")
        reply = self.say(conversation, "Not now")
        detail = "added" if self.added == ["BBL/Bambu Lab A1 mini"] else f"added {self.added or 'nothing'}"
        return self.end(reply, detail)


class ConnectOutcome(Finishing, ConnectBambu):
    """Connect the saved A1 mini, as connect-bambu does, then the person taps
    Connect on the card and the app reports the outcome in a note."""

    def connect(self, conversation, outcome):
        """The model's reply to the app's note, or None when no card came."""
        ConnectBambu.run(self, conversation)
        if not self.card:
            return None
        return last_reply(conversation, note="Connection to Bambu Lab A1 mini " + outcome)


class ConnectVerifiedClose(ConnectOutcome):
    """Passes when the reply to a verified connection says they can close the chat."""

    name = "connect-verified-close"

    def run(self, conversation):
        reply = self.connect(conversation, "verified.")
        if reply is None:
            return False, "NO CARD"
        return self.end(reply, "verified")


class ConnectLeaveClose(ConnectOutcome):
    """The connection fails and the person leaves it for now. Passes when the
    reply to that says they can close the chat."""

    name = "connect-leave-close"

1238	# --- The filament chat ---------------------------------------------------------
1239	#
1240	# The header's Filament settings… opens a chat about one filament preset with
1241	# its own instructions (filamentInstructions.ts) and the settings tools alone,
1242	# which PrinterPanel::filament_preflight holds to that preset and to saving.
1243	
1244	FILAMENT_SETTINGS = {
1245	    "nozzle_temperature": ("220,220", True, "integer[]", "Nozzle temperature"),
1246	    "nozzle_temperature_initial_layer": ("220,220", True, "integer[]", "Nozzle temperature, first layer"),
1247	    "textured_plate_temp": ("65", True, "integer[]", "Textured PEI plate temperature"),
1248	    "fan_max_speed": ("100", True, "integer[]", "Fan max speed"),
1249	    "filament_type": ("PLA", False, "string[]", "Type"),
1250	    "filament_diameter": ("1.75", False, "float[]", "Diameter"),
1251	}
1252	
1253	
1254	class FilamentCase:
1255	    """A filament chat about one preset, its settings tools answered as the app
1256	    answers them: PrinterPanel::filament_preflight, then OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.
1257	    The preset is the one open in its settings tab, and in slot 1."""
1258	
1259	    preset = "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C"
1260	    shown = "Bambu PLA Basic"
1261	    stock = True
1262	    tools = [tool for tool in TOOLS if tool["name"] in SETTINGS]
1263	
1264	    def __init__(self):
1265	        self.calls = []
1266	
1267	    @classmethod
1268	    def session_for(cls):
1269	        session = {"kind": "filament", "slot": 1, "preset": cls.preset, "shown": cls.shown, "material": "PLA",
1270	                   "stock": cls.stock}
1271	        if cls.stock:
1272	            session["copyName"] = cls.preset + " - Copy"
1273	        return session
1274	
1275	    def tool(self, name, arguments):
1276	        self.calls.append((name, arguments))
1277	        own = self.preset
1278	        if problem := invalid_arguments(name, arguments):
1279	            return {"error": problem}, False
1280	        if arguments.get("scope") != "filament" or (arguments.get("target") or {}).get("preset") != own:
1281	            return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_conversation", "message": "This chat changes the settings of one filament: "
1282	                                                                             f'pass scope filament and target.preset "{own}".'}}, False
1283	        if name == "settings_apply_patch" and "persistAs" not in arguments:
1284	            return {"error": {"code": "not_saved", "message": f'Every change in this chat is saved: pass persistAs "{own}", or '
1285	                                                              "the copy's name a read_only_preset issue gives."}}, False
1286	        context = {"scope": "filament", "presetName": own, "sessionId": "1", "revision": 7, "truncated": False}
1287	        if name == "settings_search":
1288	            words = [w for w in re.split(r"[\s,;]+", str(arguments.get("query", "")).lower()) if w]
1289	            items = [{"key": key, "type": kind, "label": label, "category": "Filament", "description": label, "unit": "",
1290	                      "enumValues": [], "enumLabels": [], "writable": writable, "truncated": False}
1291	                     for key, (_, writable, kind, label) in FILAMENT_SETTINGS.items()
1292	                     if not words or any(w in key or w in label.lower() for w in words)]
1293	            return {**context, "items": items, "nextCursor": ""}, False
1294	        if name == "settings_get":
1295	            items, unknown = [], []
1296	            for key in arguments.get("keys", []):
1297	                if key in FILAMENT_SETTINGS:
1298	                    value, writable, kind, label = FILAMENT_SETTINGS[key]
1299	                    items.append({"key": key, "value": value, "type": kind, "label": label, "unit": "",
1300	                                  "differsFromPreset": False, "differsFromSystem": False, "writable": writable})
1301	                else:
1302	                    unknown.append({"key": key, "code": "unknown_setting", "message": "Unknown setting.", "allowed": [],
1303	                                    "suggestions": [], "truncated": False})
1304	            return {**context, "items": items, "unknownKeys": unknown}, False
1305	        issues, changes = [], []
1306	        for key, value in (arguments.get("changes") or {}).items():
1307	            if key not in FILAMENT_SETTINGS:
1308	                issues.append({"key": key, "code": "unknown_setting", "message": "Unknown setting."})
1309	            elif not FILAMENT_SETTINGS[key][1]:
1310	                issues.append({"key": key, "code": "unsupported_setting_mutation", "message": "This filament setting is read-only."})
1311	            elif len(str(value).split(",")) != len(FILAMENT_SETTINGS[key][0].split(",")):
1312	                count = len(FILAMENT_SETTINGS[key][0].split(","))
1313	                issues.append({"key": key, "code": "invalid_setting_value",
1314	                               "message": f"This setting holds {count} values; give {count}, separated by commas."})
1315	            else:
1316	                changes.append({"key": key, "before": FILAMENT_SETTINGS[key][0], "after": str(value)})
1317	        persist = arguments.get("persistAs")
1318	        if not issues and persist == own and self.stock:
1319	            issues.append({"key": "", "code": "read_only_preset", "suggestions": [own + " - Copy"],
1320	                           "message": f'"{own}" comes with OrcaSlicer and cannot be overwritten. Save the change as a copy: '
1321	                                      f'pass persistAs "{own} - Copy".'})
1322	        if name == "settings_preview_patch":
1323	            return {**context, "valid": not issues, "changes": changes if not issues else [], "dependencies": [],
1324	                    "issues": issues, "warnings": []}, False
1325	        if issues:
1326	            return {"error": {"code": issues[0]["code"], "message": issues[0]["message"]}}, False
1327	        return {**context, "applied": True, "changes": changes, "normalized": [],
1328	                "savedAs": persist or "", "presetDirty": persist is None,
1329	                "projectUndo": False, "truncated": False}, False
1330	
1331	    def called(self, *names):
1332	        return [(name, arguments) for name, arguments in self.calls if name in names]
1333	
1334	    def applied(self):
1335	        return [arguments for _, arguments in self.called("settings_apply_patch")]

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 16 14:18:43 2026 -0700

    Judge and answer every tool call in a project prompt test response
    
    The project prompt runner kept only the first function_call of each model
    response. When a response held several, the later ones were neither
    judged nor answered, and they stayed in the history without a result. On
    2026-10-16, in petg-on-cool-plate, a response held workspace_inspect and
    an intent_update with a purpose the person never gave; the read was
    answered and the change was never looked at. A case that fails on "a
    change" could pass when the change came second.
    
    The runner now judges a response the way the app now runs it:
    - A change anywhere in the response is the step (the first change, if
      several), and nothing is answered.
    - A response of reads only is checked read by read, and the first read
      the case decides on is the outcome.
    - When the case decides on none of them, every read is answered from the
      recording, each under its own call id, in order. If any read has no
      recorded answer, none is answered and the run ends unobserved. A read
      after one whose result did not succeed gets the app's "not run" result.
    - A run's report lists every call of the response it ended on.
    
    MAX_READS now counts responses, so a run still sends at most four
    requests. The prompt and every case's check are unchanged; two docstrings
    that said "the first call" now say "the first response".
    
    test_steps.py checks this offline with hand-written model outputs and no
    key: 13 tests, 8 of which fail on the previous runner, plus a check that
    the runner's "not run" text matches the app's source byte for byte.
    --render-only sends the same 25 bodies as before apart from the flag.
    
    requests.json is recorded again for the app's parallel_tool_calls: true.
    Only that flag, ids, timestamps and a temporary path changed.
    print-this-no-purpose is again recorded on its own, as in the commit that
    added its fixture: recorded after the other conversations, its project
    reports unsaved changes and a slice handle, which it did not when its
    runs were measured. The README describes the rule and the recording.
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M5399QN3818M8NVWZ4RSGN2B

"""The runner's handling of the model's responses, offline: hand-written
outputs in place of the model, no key and no request sent. Above all a
response with several calls, which the runner once judged and answered by
its first call alone.

Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py

import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import re
import unittest

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run_prompt_tests", HERE / "run_prompt_tests.py")
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)


def call(name, arguments=None, call_id=None):
    return {"type": "function_call", "call_id": call_id or "call-" + name, "name": name,
            "arguments": json.dumps(arguments or {})}


def reply(text):
    return {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": text}]}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The runner's handling of the model's responses, offline: hand-written
outputs in place of the model, no key and no request sent. Above all a
response with several calls, of which the runner once answered only the
first.

Usage: python3 tests/printer_prompt/test_responses.py
"""

import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import re
import unittest

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run_prompt_tests", HERE / "run_prompt_tests.py")
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)

PROMPT = {"instructions": "instructions", "opening": "Which printer is it?"}
FILAMENT = "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C"
KOBRA = runner.KOBRA["name"]


def call(name, arguments=None, call_id=None):
    return {"type": "function_call", "call_id": call_id or "call-" + name, "name": name,
            "arguments": json.dumps(arguments or {})}


def reply(text):
    return {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": text}]}


def apply_start_gcode(persist_as=None, call_id=None):
    arguments = {"scope": "printer", "target": {"preset": KOBRA}, "expectedSessionId": "1", "expectedRevision": 7,
                 "changes": {"machine_start_gcode": "G28 ; home all axes\nG29\nG1 Z5 F5000 ; lift nozzle"}}
    if persist_as:
        arguments["persistAs"] = persist_as
    return call("settings_apply_patch", arguments, call_id)


class Scripted:
    """The model, as a list of outputs, one per request; keeps each request."""

    def __init__(self, *outputs):
        self.outputs, self.bodies = list(outputs), []

    def __call__(self, body, key, endpoint=None):
        self.bodies.append(json.loads(json.dumps(body)))  # as sent, before the runner adds to its input
        return {"output": self.outputs.pop(0)}


class Responses(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.post, self.judge = runner.post, runner.judge
        runner.judge = lambda log, question: self.fail("no case here should need the judge")

    def tearDown(self):
        runner.post, runner.judge = self.post, self.judge

    def run_case(self, case_class, *outputs):
        """A run as run_once makes it, with the case it ran and the requests
        it sent."""
        kept = []

        class Kept(case_class):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                kept.append(self)

        runner.post = Scripted(*outputs)
        passed, detail, log = runner.run_once(Kept, PROMPT, "key", "model")
        bodies = runner.post.bodies
        self.assertTrue(all(body["parallel_tool_calls"] is True for body in bodies))
        self.assertEqual(runner.post.outputs, [], "every scripted output is used")
        return passed, detail, kept[0], bodies

    @staticmethod
    def results(body):
        return {item["call_id"]: json.loads(item["output"]) for item in body["input"] if item.get("type") == "function_call_output"}

    # --- Every call of a response runs -------------------------------------

    def test_a_change_after_a_read_runs(self):
        """A read and the change after it in one response: both run, in order,
        and both results go back in one request. The runner once answered the
        read alone, and the change never reached the simulator."""
        changes = {"nozzle_temperature": "225,225", "nozzle_temperature_initial_layer": "225,225"}
        first = [{"type": "reasoning", "id": "r-1", "summary": []},
                 call("settings_get", {"scope": "filament", "target": {"preset": FILAMENT},
                                       "keys": ["nozzle_temperature", "nozzle_temperature_initial_layer"]}, "call-a"),
                 call("settings_apply_patch", {"scope": "filament", "target": {"preset": FILAMENT}, "changes": changes,
                                               "expectedSessionId": "1", "expectedRevision": 7,
                                               "persistAs": FILAMENT + " - Copy"}, "call-b")]
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(runner.FilamentHotter, first,
                                                     [reply("It now prints at 225 °C, saved as your own copy.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual([name for name, _ in case.calls], ["settings_get", "settings_apply_patch"])
        self.assertEqual(len(bodies), 2)
        sent = bodies[1]["input"]
        start = len(sent) - len(first) - 2
        self.assertEqual(sent[start:start + len(first)], first)
        outputs = sent[start + len(first):]
        self.assertEqual([(item["type"], item["call_id"]) for item in outputs],
                         [("function_call_output", "call-a"), ("function_call_output", "call-b")])
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(outputs[1]["output"])["savedAs"], FILAMENT + " - Copy")

    def test_a_call_after_a_failed_one_is_not_run(self):
        """The first change fails (no persistAs on a printer the project does
        not use), so the second is answered not_run and never reaches the
        simulator; the model calls it again in its next response."""
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ChangeEditStartGcode,
            [apply_start_gcode(None, "call-1"), apply_start_gcode(KOBRA, "call-2")],
            [apply_start_gcode(KOBRA, "call-3")],
            [reply("Added G29 after G28 and saved it.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual([arguments.get("persistAs") for arguments in case.applied()], [None, KOBRA])
        results = self.results(bodies[1])
        self.assertEqual(results["call-1"]["error"]["code"], "not_selected")
        self.assertEqual(results["call-2"], {"state": "failed", "error": {"code": "not_run", "message":
                         "Not run: an earlier call in the same response, settings_apply_patch (call-1), did not succeed. "
                         "Nothing was queued. Call it again if it is still needed."}})
        self.assertTrue(self.results(bodies[2])["call-3"]["applied"])

    def test_a_refused_call_stops_the_calls_after_it(self):
        """A call to no tool is refused before it runs, which is a call that
        did not succeed: the change after it is not run."""
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ChangeAskNozzle,
            [call("printer_details", {}, "call-x"), call("printer_change", {"printerName": KOBRA, "nozzle": 0.6}, "call-y")],
            [reply("It is set up for a 0.4 mm nozzle.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(case.calls, [])
        results = self.results(bodies[1])
        self.assertEqual(results["call-x"]["error"]["code"], "unknown_tool")
        self.assertEqual(results["call-y"]["error"]["code"], "not_run")
        self.assertIn("printer_details (call-x)", results["call-y"]["error"]["message"])

    def test_calls_after_a_success_keep_running(self):
        """credential_requested is a success: nothing after it is held back."""
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ConnectBambu,
            [call("printer_connect", {"deviceId": "FAKE001"}, "call-c"), call("printer_connection_status", {}, "call-s")],
            [reply("Enter the access code from the printer's screen in the form.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(case.other, ["printer_connection_status"])  # ConnectBambu answers it as untested, but it ran
        self.assertEqual(self.results(bodies[1])["call-c"]["state"], "credential_requested")

    # --- What later turns replay -------------------------------------------

    def test_the_next_turn_replays_the_calls_that_ran(self):
        """Every call that ran is replayed in the next turn, each with its
        result, in order; the one answered not_run is not, since the app never
        ran or recorded it."""
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ConnectBambu,
            [call("printer_connection_status", {}, "call-s"), call("printer_connect", {"deviceId": "<from_status>"}, "call-bad"),
             call("printer_connect", {"deviceId": "FAKE001"}, "call-unrun")],
            [reply("I couldn't find it. Is it in LAN mode?\nChoices: Yes | No")],
            [call("printer_connect", {"deviceId": "FAKE001"}, "call-ok")],
            [reply("Enter the access code from the printer's screen in the form.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(case.refused, ["<from_status>"])
        self.assertEqual(self.results(bodies[1])["call-unrun"]["error"]["code"], "not_run")
        next_turn = bodies[2]["input"]
        self.assertEqual(next_turn[-1], {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Yes, connect it"}]})
        replayed = [(item["type"], item["call_id"]) for item in next_turn if "call_id" in item]
        self.assertEqual(replayed, [("function_call", "call-s"), ("function_call_output", "call-s"),
                                    ("function_call", "call-bad"), ("function_call_output", "call-bad")])
        self.assertTrue(all("id" not in item for item in next_turn if item.get("type") == "function_call"))

    # --- One call or none, as before ---------------------------------------

    def test_a_single_call_then_a_reply(self):
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ChangeNozzleClose,
            [call("printer_change", {"printerName": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "nozzle": 0.6}, "call-1")],
            [reply("Saved: it now has a 0.6 mm nozzle. You can close this chat.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(bodies[1]["input"][-1]["call_id"], "call-1")

    def test_a_reply_ends_the_turn(self):
        passed, detail, _, bodies = self.run_case(runner.ChangeLoadedFilament, [reply("Nothing to save for that.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(len(bodies), 1)

    # --- The app's own words and rule --------------------------------------

    def test_the_unrun_result_is_the_apps_own(self):
        """The runner's "not run" text is the app's, word for word."""
        source = (HERE.parents[1] / "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        block = source[source.index('"Not run:'):source.index('still needed."') + len('still needed."')]
        head, *rest = re.findall(r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"', block)
        expected = {"state": "failed", "error": {"code": "not_run", "message": head + "printer_add (call-p)" + "".join(rest)}}
        self.assertEqual(runner.dump(runner.not_run("printer_add (call-p)")), runner.dump(expected))

    def test_what_counts_as_succeeded(self):
        self.assertTrue(runner.succeeded({"state": "credential_requested", "message": "waiting"}))
        self.assertTrue(runner.succeeded({"printers": []}))
        self.assertFalse(runner.succeeded({"error": {"code": "unknown_device", "message": "..."}}))
        self.assertFalse(runner.succeeded({"state": "failed", "error": {"code": "invalid_arguments"}}))
        self.assertFalse(runner.succeeded({"state": "cancelled"}))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

        """A run as run_once makes it, with the case it ran and the requests
        it sent."""
        kept = []

        class Kept(case_class):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                kept.append(self)

        runner.post = Scripted(*outputs)
        passed, detail, log = runner.run_once(Kept, PROMPT, "key", "model")
        bodies = runner.post.bodies
        self.assertTrue(all(body["parallel_tool_calls"] is True for body in bodies))
        self.assertEqual(runner.post.outputs, [], "every scripted output is used")
        return passed, detail, kept[0], bodies

    @staticmethod
    def results(body):
        return {item["call_id"]: json.loads(item["output"]) for item in body["input"] if item.get("type") == "function_call_output"}

    # --- Every call of a response runs -------------------------------------

    def test_a_change_after_a_read_runs(self):
        """A read and the change after it in one response: both run, in order,
        and both results go back in one request. The runner once answered the
        read alone, and the change never reached the simulator."""
        changes = {"nozzle_temperature": "225,225", "nozzle_temperature_initial_layer": "225,225"}
        first = [{"type": "reasoning", "id": "r-1", "summary": []},
                 call("settings_get", {"scope": "filament", "target": {"preset": FILAMENT},
                                       "keys": ["nozzle_temperature", "nozzle_temperature_initial_layer"]}, "call-a"),
                 call("settings_apply_patch", {"scope": "filament", "target": {"preset": FILAMENT}, "changes": changes,
                                               "expectedSessionId": "1", "expectedRevision": 7,
                                               "persistAs": FILAMENT + " - Copy"}, "call-b")]
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(runner.FilamentHotter, first,
                                                     [reply("It now prints at 225 °C, saved as your own copy.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual([name for name, _ in case.calls], ["settings_get", "settings_apply_patch"])
        self.assertEqual(len(bodies), 2)
        sent = bodies[1]["input"]
        start = len(sent) - len(first) - 2
        self.assertEqual(sent[start:start + len(first)], first)
        outputs = sent[start + len(first):]
        self.assertEqual([(item["type"], item["call_id"]) for item in outputs],
                         [("function_call_output", "call-a"), ("function_call_output", "call-b")])
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(outputs[1]["output"])["savedAs"], FILAMENT + " - Copy")

    def test_a_call_after_a_failed_one_is_not_run(self):
        """The first change fails (no persistAs on a printer the project does
        not use), so the second is answered not_run and never reaches the
        simulator; the model calls it again in its next response."""
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ChangeEditStartGcode,
            [apply_start_gcode(None, "call-1"), apply_start_gcode(KOBRA, "call-2")],
            [apply_start_gcode(KOBRA, "call-3")],
            [reply("Added G29 after G28 and saved it.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual([arguments.get("persistAs") for arguments in case.applied()], [None, KOBRA])
        results = self.results(bodies[1])
        self.assertEqual(results["call-1"]["error"]["code"], "not_selected")
        self.assertEqual(results["call-2"], {"state": "failed", "error": {"code": "not_run", "message":
                         "Not run: an earlier call in the same response, settings_apply_patch (call-1), did not succeed. "
                         "Nothing was queued. Call it again if it is still needed."}})
        self.assertTrue(self.results(bodies[2])["call-3"]["applied"])

    def test_a_refused_call_stops_the_calls_after_it(self):
        """A call to no tool is refused before it runs, which is a call that
        did not succeed: the change after it is not run."""
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ChangeAskNozzle,
            [call("printer_details", {}, "call-x"), call("printer_change", {"printerName": KOBRA, "nozzle": 0.6}, "call-y")],
            [reply("It is set up for a 0.4 mm nozzle.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(case.calls, [])
        results = self.results(bodies[1])
        self.assertEqual(results["call-x"]["error"]["code"], "unknown_tool")
        self.assertEqual(results["call-y"]["error"]["code"], "not_run")
        self.assertIn("printer_details (call-x)", results["call-y"]["error"]["message"])

    def test_calls_after_a_success_keep_running(self):
        """credential_requested is a success: nothing after it is held back."""
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ConnectBambu,
            [call("printer_connect", {"deviceId": "FAKE001"}, "call-c"), call("printer_connection_status", {}, "call-s")],
            [reply("Enter the access code from the printer's screen in the form.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(case.other, ["printer_connection_status"])  # ConnectBambu answers it as untested, but it ran
        self.assertEqual(self.results(bodies[1])["call-c"]["state"], "credential_requested")

    # --- What later turns replay -------------------------------------------

    def test_the_next_turn_replays_the_calls_that_ran(self):
        """Every call that ran is replayed in the next turn, each with its
        result, in order; the one answered not_run is not, since the app never
        ran or recorded it."""
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ConnectBambu,
            [call("printer_connection_status", {}, "call-s"), call("printer_connect", {"deviceId": "<from_status>"}, "call-bad"),
             call("printer_connect", {"deviceId": "FAKE001"}, "call-unrun")],
            [reply("I couldn't find it. Is it in LAN mode?\nChoices: Yes | No")],
            [call("printer_connect", {"deviceId": "FAKE001"}, "call-ok")],
            [reply("Enter the access code from the printer's screen in the form.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(case.refused, ["<from_status>"])
        self.assertEqual(self.results(bodies[1])["call-unrun"]["error"]["code"], "not_run")
        next_turn = bodies[2]["input"]
        self.assertEqual(next_turn[-1], {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Yes, connect it"}]})
        replayed = [(item["type"], item["call_id"]) for item in next_turn if "call_id" in item]
        self.assertEqual(replayed, [("function_call", "call-s"), ("function_call_output", "call-s"),
                                    ("function_call", "call-bad"), ("function_call_output", "call-bad")])
        self.assertTrue(all("id" not in item for item in next_turn if item.get("type") == "function_call"))

    # --- One call or none, as before ---------------------------------------

    def test_a_single_call_then_a_reply(self):
        passed, detail, case, bodies = self.run_case(
            runner.ChangeNozzleClose,
            [call("printer_change", {"printerName": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "nozzle": 0.6}, "call-1")],
            [reply("Saved: it now has a 0.6 mm nozzle. You can close this chat.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(bodies[1]["input"][-1]["call_id"], "call-1")

    def test_a_reply_ends_the_turn(self):
        passed, detail, _, bodies = self.run_case(runner.ChangeLoadedFilament, [reply("Nothing to save for that.")])
        self.assertTrue(passed, detail)
        self.assertEqual(len(bodies), 1)

    # --- The app's own words and rule --------------------------------------

    def test_the_unrun_result_is_the_apps_own(self):
        """The runner's "not run" text is the app's, word for word."""
        source = (HERE.parents[1] / "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        block = source[source.index('"Not run:'):source.index('still needed."') + len('still needed."')]
        head, *rest = re.findall(r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"', block)
        expected = {"state": "failed", "error": {"code": "not_run", "message": head + "printer_add (call-p)" + "".join(rest)}}
        self.assertEqual(runner.dump(runner.not_run("printer_add (call-p)")), runner.dump(expected))

    def test_what_counts_as_succeeded(self):
        self.assertTrue(runner.succeeded({"state": "credential_requested", "message": "waiting"}))
        self.assertTrue(runner.succeeded({"printers": []}))
        self.assertFalse(runner.succeeded({"error": {"code": "unknown_device", "message": "..."}}))
        self.assertFalse(runner.succeeded({"state": "failed", "error": {"code": "invalid_arguments"}}))
        self.assertFalse(runner.succeeded({"state": "cancelled"}))

Answer every tool call in a printer prompt test response

The app's OpenAI adapter now asks for several tool calls per response
(parallel_tool_calls: true) and runs every one, in the order the model
wrote it. The printer prompt runner still asked for one call and
answered only the first function_call of a response. Any later calls
got no result and never reached the printer simulator. So a change
written after a read in the same response was never made, and the case
judged a conversation the app would not have had.

The runner now sends parallel_tool_calls: true and answers every call
of a response from its simulator, in order, each under its own call id.
All the results go back in one request. A call can fail in two ways:
the simulator answers it with an error, or the runner refuses it for

content.text:
The printer prompt test runner now matches the app: it sends `parallel_tool_calls: true` and answers every tool call in a model response, in order, from its printer simulator. Once a call fails, every later call in that response gets the app's `not_run` result without running. I tested this offline with hand-written model outputs only; no live model was called and no key was read.

**Where it is:** commit `0ad542da6d` on a new branch, `claude/printer-every-tool-call`, in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/printer-every-tool-call`. I based it on `claude/every-tool-call` because that branch isn't merged into `jusprin-newui` yet. Nothing is pushed.

**What changed in `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`:**
- Every call in a response is answered under its own call id, and all the results go back together in the next request.
- A call counts as failed if the simulator's answer has an `error` key or a `failed`/`cancelled` state. Calls the runner refuses for bad arguments or an unknown tool also count as failed. I chose the `error` key because the app's printer panel reports a failed printer tool as `{"error": …}` with no `state` field (`PrinterConversation::tool_output`).
- Calls after a failure get the `not_run` text from `OpenAIResponsesAgent::next_call`, word for word. They never reach the simulator, and later turns don't replay them, because the app never runs or records them either.

**Case checks:** none changed. No check reads only the first call; each one reads what the simulator was asked over the whole conversation. One thing you may want to revisit: a call answered `not_run` never reaches the simulator, so a check ignores it. For example, a forbidden `printer_add` that comes after a failed call doesn't fail the run. Calls refused for bad arguments were already ignored the same way.

**Tests:** I added `tests/printer_prompt/test_responses.py` (run it with `python3 tests/printer_prompt/test_responses.py`). All 9 tests pass. Against the old runner, 7 fail because of how it handled the calls. The other 2 have only one call per response, so on the old runner they fail only on the flag. One test checks that the runner's `not_run` text matches the app's C++ source exactly.

**README:** it now has a paragraph describing the rule, in the same style as the rest. It also notes that pass counts recorded before 2026-10-16 came from a runner that answered only the first call, so comparisons should use before-and-after runs made with this runner.

One older difference remains, and I left it alone: after two refused calls in one turn, the app ends the turn, but the runner passes the next bad call to the simulator instead.

class AfterPreview(Case):
    """The prepare turn after settings_preview_patch returned a valid preview.
    Line 12: "When asked to make a supported change, call the matching tool"
    and "Use only IDs from current authoritative workspace context or tool
    results." Passes on settings_apply_patch with the preview's sessionId and
    revision; fails on any other change or a reply."""

    name = "after-preview"

    def check(self, step):
        preview = last_result(self.request)["result"]
        if step.tool == "settings_apply_patch" and step.arguments.get("expectedSessionId") == preview["sessionId"] and \
                step.arguments.get("expectedRevision") == preview["revision"]:
            return PASS, str(step)
        if step.reads():
            return CONTINUE, str(step)
        return FAIL, f"{step} (preview {preview['sessionId']}/{preview['revision']})"


class Readiness(Case):
    """Shared by the two verification cases: the expected call passes, a reply
    passes unless the judge reads a claim that the print is ready."""

    expected = None

    def check(self, step):
        if step.tool == self.expected:
            return PASS, str(step)
        if step.reads():
            return CONTINUE, str(step)
        if step.tool:
